findings: The hero's glowing orange light-arch on black is the weakest single asset — it reads close to a generic AI atmospheric render and its brightness nearly out-competes the name for first focal landing.

The density of tiny monospace annotations (plate numbers, 'the sun 87° up', exposure logs) occasionally tips toward decoration-as-texture; a stricter edit would let a few breathe instead of carpeting the dark bands.
The vertical amber streak bands in §4 ('plate iii') read as abstract generative filler that is hard to parse as anything beyond mood — borderline garnish within an otherwise disciplined system.
what_works: Genuine high-contrast Didone display/serif paired against a monospace utility voice — exactly the editorial pairing a templated generator avoids, deployed consistently (the italic 'Analemma' and 'stood still' / 'comes back' accents are confident).

A committed conceptual throughline (Daguerre's long-exposure plate / 'the one man who stood still', a generation counter, the ghosted multi-face self-portrait composite in §3, the analemma spiral drawing) — this is editorial conviction, not a feature grid.
Asymmetric split hero: large name top-left over cream against a dark photographic panel, with off-axis mono metadata — a deliberate composition, not a centered headline over gradient.
Single warm amber accent governed by the exposure concept, held against near-black and cream; disciplined rather than a rainbow or purple-blue default.

Stranger test fully satisfied in the first viewport: name 'André Macedo' huge, one line on what he does (co-founder of RealWorld.fi and ActualSales), and me@andremacedo.com all legible without scrolling.
A.reasoning: This is clearly not SaaS slop: it reads as an editorial art object with a high-contrast serif + mono type system, an asymmetric photographic hero, and a sustained daguerreotype/long-exposure conceptual throughline that a template would never produce. No cardinal slop state is present — no centered gradient hero, no default sans, no feature-card grid, and there is a decisive signature move. It loses points only for the slightly generic glowing-arch hero image, occasional mono-annotation clutter, and a couple of abstract filler bands, keeping it at a solid pass rather than an exceptional one.

B.reasoning: This is competent but mediocre default-grade AI art-website slop. The hero is the strongest element (hence 7), but the page fails the stranger_test floor (no clear 'what he does' or contact in first viewport), exhibits multiple cardinal slop states including template shape, decorative atmospheric effects without tight hierarchy, and symmetry-as-substitute in the stacked sections. No visible modular type scale or signature compositional risk elevates it beyond generic 'poetic personal site' output. The living-organism conceit is told more than shown in the pixels.
